question: Of the \(500\) balls in a large bag, \(80\%\) are red and the rest are blue. How many of the red balls must be removed so that \(75\%\) of the remaining balls are red?
solution:
Only red balls are removed, so the number of blue balls stays fixed. Initially, blue balls make up \(100\%-80\%=20\%\) of the bag, giving
\[
0.20\cdot500=100\text{ blue balls}.
\]
When \(75\%\) of the remaining balls are red, the other \(25\%\) are blue. Thus the unchanged \(100\) blue balls are \(25\%\) of the remaining total. That total must be
\[
100\div0.25=400\text{ balls}.
\]
The number removed is \(500-400=\boxed{100}\), all red. Indeed, the remaining bag has \(300\) red and \(100\) blue balls, so its red share is \(300/400=75\%\). The answer is choice D.
